issues.concern: The headword '者' (mono) is not inherently formal. While it can be used in formal contexts, it is also very common in neutral and even informal speech, especially in compounds or as a general pronoun for 'person.' The 'formal/written' nuance is more about the *usage* of the word in certain phrases or as a general noun, rather than the word itself being inherently formal.
The gloss incorrectly labels the word as 'formal/written.' While it can appear in formal/written contexts, the word itself is not inherently formal and is used broadly.
